#!/bin/sh
# Entire CLI local-development hook launcher.
#
# In local-dev mode, Entire hooks invoke the CLI straight from source via
# "go run", which recompiles on demand. When the tree does not compile (for
# example while an agent is resolving a merge conflict) "go run" fails and the
# hook would silently do nothing. This launcher first checks that the tree
# builds; if it does it runs the freshly compiled CLI, otherwise it falls back
# to an "entire" binary on PATH. If neither is available it exits 0 so it never
# blocks the surrounding git or agent operation.
#
# Usage: scripts/entire-dev <entire args...>
#
# All local-dev hooks delegate here so the build-probe-and-fallback logic lives
# in one place rather than being duplicated across generated hook commands.

set -eu

# Informational messages go to stderr so they never pollute hook stdout (some
# hooks emit JSON there).
log() {
	printf '[entire-dev] %s\n' "$1" >&2
}

# Resolve the repository root from this script's own location so it works
# regardless of the caller's working directory. Parameter expansion avoids
# depending on external tools like dirname, which may not be on PATH when this
# runs from a minimal hook environment.
case "$0" in
	*/*) script_dir=${0%/*} ;;
	*) script_dir=. ;;
esac
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
# Build/run the whole cmd/entire package, not just main.go: package main is
# split across multiple files (e.g. the git-remote-entire dispatch in
# remotehelper.go), and naming a single file would leave the others out and
# fail to compile.
pkg="$root/cmd/entire"

# Run freshly compiled code when the tree builds. The build probe populates the
# build cache, so the subsequent "go run" does not recompile from scratch.
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 && go build -o /dev/null "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	exec go run "$pkg" "$@"
fi

# The tree does not build (or Go is unavailable): fall back to the installed
# binary so hooks keep working while the source is broken.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "project isn't compiling; falling back to the entire binary on PATH"
	exec entire "$@"
fi

# Nothing to run: do not block the surrounding operation.
log "project isn't compiling and no entire binary on PATH; skipping hook"
exit 0

## What's happening

Your `e2e/artifacts/` directory has grown to **19,071 files across 15,364 directories** (114 MB, 45 canary runs going back to May). It's correctly gitignored (`.gitignore:53`) — but go-git doesn't skip it.

Measured in your repo right now:

| operation | time |
|---|---|
| `git status --porcelain` (CLI) | 0.013s |
| go-git `worktree.Status()` | **5.25s** |
| `gitignore.ReadPatterns` alone | 2.81s — of which **1.75s is descending `e2e/artifacts` to find 0 patterns** |
| go-git `Status()` with artifacts moved aside | **0.065s** (80× faster) |

go-git's `Worktree.Status()` recursively walks every directory looking for nested `.gitignore` files *before* it can apply ignore rules, then walks the tree again for untracked files. 15,364 throwaway directories get fully traversed twice.

Then the UserPromptSubmit hook calls it **twice** — `DetectFileChanges` (`cmd/entire/cli/state.go:277`) and `getUntrackedFilesForState` (`cmd/entire/cli/state.go:448`), each opening the repo independently. That's the two ~5.2s gaps I see in the debug log:

```
  0.000  lifecycle    turn-start
  5.257  session      ApplyTransition
  0.000  session      phase transition
  5.184  hooks        initialized shadow session
```

End-to-end the hook takes **~11.4s** of which 9.8s is system (syscall) time — pure directory walking.

**Why it tips over 30s rather than just being slow:** this repo has `"local_dev": true`, so hooks run via `scripts/entire-dev`, which does `go build` *then* `go run` on every invocation. Warm that's ~1s. But your last commit (`773db0d34`) bumped Go 1.26.4 → 1.26.5, which invalidates the entire build cache — the first hook after that rebuilds the whole dependency tree. 11s of tree-walking plus a cold Go rebuild clears 30s easily. I didn't measure the cold rebuild since it'd mean wiping your build cache.

Note `.git` is also 3.1 GB with 116 packfiles (one 2.0 GB) — not the cause here, but worth knowing.

The one-line unblock is clearing the artifacts — that alone takes the hook from ~11s to under 1s:

```bash
rm -rf e2e/artifacts/*
```

I've left that to you since it's destructive, even though the contents are disposable canary output.

Raising the hook `timeout` would just hide it. The durable fixes, in order of value:

1. **Use `git status --porcelain` instead of go-git for these two call sites** — 400× faster, and consistent with the existing precedent in CLAUDE.md of avoiding go-git for worktree operations it handles badly.
2. **Share one `Status()` per hook invocation** instead of two independent repo opens.
3. **Prune `e2e/artifacts` in the canary task** so it can't accumulate again.

`Worktree.Status()` collects ignore rules via `gitignore.ReadPatterns`, which blindly attempts to open `<dir>/.gitignore` **and** `<dir>/.git/info/exclude` at every directory it recurses into — even though the `ReadDir` listing it already holds answers whether those files exist. On `BoundOS` filesystems each failed open pays a full path-traversal cost; in the #181 investigation profile these failed opens dominated `ReadPatterns`, which itself accounted for ~28% of `Status()` CPU on a home-directory-style worktree.

Reference git reads a directory's `.gitignore` only when it exists, and consults `$GIT_DIR/info/exclude` only of the repository being walked ([`dir.c` `setup_standard_excludes()`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/dir.c)).

## What

- `ReadPatterns` now runs `ReadDir` first and opens `.gitignore` only when it appears in the listing. Directories without ignore files — the overwhelming common case — cost a single `ReadDir`, with zero open attempts.
- `.git/info/exclude` is read only at the root of the walked filesystem, and only when `.git` is present there. This also fixes a semantic divergence: a nested `<dir>/.git/info/exclude` (e.g. an embedded repository) previously contributed patterns to the outer walk; reference git never does that.
- Public API unchanged. One subtlety: on `ReadDir` error the function now returns `nil` patterns instead of partially-read ones; the sole caller (`collectIgnorePatterns`) discards patterns on error, so behavior is unchanged.

This is an independent follow-up to #2282 (stacks on `main`, not on that branch); the larger "lazy/incremental pattern walk" idea mentioned there remains future work.

## Benchmarks

New `BenchmarkReadPatterns` over 1,100 directories with no ignore files in subdirectories (home-directory-like worst case), `osfs` with `BoundOS` on an Apple M4 Pro. A/B of `main` vs this branch, 7 runs each (`-benchtime=3x`), via `benchstat`:

## What the PR does

[go-git#2284](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2284) (merged 2026-07-30) makes `ReadPatterns` call `ReadDir` first and open `.gitignore` only when it's actually in the listing, instead of blindly attempting to open `<dir>/.gitignore` and `<dir>/.git/info/exclude` in every directory. It also scopes `.git/info/exclude` to the walk root, matching reference git.

It's real and it helps us — that's the exact function I measured at 2.26s. **We don't have it:** `alpha.5` was tagged 2026-07-29 11:36, the PR was opened at 17:12 the same day. `alpha.5` is still the newest tag, so it's `main`-only.

I benchmarked both against your actual repo:

| | ReadPatterns | `Worktree.Status()` |
|---|---|---|
| alpha.5 (what we use) | 2.26s | 5.24s |
| go-git `main` @ cf4d91c7 (#2284) | 0.85s | **2.47s** |

A genuine 2.1×. It would take the hook from ~11.4s to ~6s — under the 30s timeout, but still ~190× slower than `git status`.

## But it doesn't fix our actual bug

Chasing this turned up the real defect, which #2284 leaves untouched. `ReadPatterns` recurses with `ReadPatterns(fs, append(path, fi.Name()))` — it never passes the accumulated patterns down. Each recursive call rebuilds `ps` from only that directory's own ignore files. So the prune check `NewMatcher(ps).Match(...)` can only ever match patterns from the current directory, not inherited ones.

Consequence: **an ignore rule prunes the walk only if its target is a direct child of the `.gitignore` that declares it.** Same 3,000-directory tree, on go-git `main`:

- root `.gitignore` = `big/` → **0ms**, pruned correctly
- root `.gitignore` = `e2e/artifacts/` → **121ms**, full descent into all 3,000 dirs

Reference git treats both identically. Ours is the second shape — `e2e/artifacts/` at `.gitignore:53` is one level too deep to ever prune, which is why go-git walks all 15,364 directories. The PR author flags this as unfixed: *"the larger 'lazy/incremental pattern walk' idea mentioned there remains future work."*

## The much better fix

Moving the rule so it's a direct child of its `.gitignore` sidesteps the whole thing. On your real repo, **with the current alpha.5 dependency, no upgrade**:

```bash

```

| | ReadPatterns | `Worktree.Status()` |
|---|---|---|
| alpha.5 today | 2.26s | 5.24s |
| alpha.5 + `e2e/.gitignore` | 0.02s | **0.045s** |

**116×**, versus 2.1× from the upgrade. Semantically identical to git — `artifacts/` in `e2e/.gitignore` means exactly what `e2e/artifacts/` in the root one means. One committed line, no dependency bump, and it survives artifacts re-accumulating.

1. **`e2e/.gitignore`** — one line, 116×, fixes it today.
2. **Still cut the two `Status()` calls to one** (`state.go:277`, `state.go:448`) — halves whatever remains.
3. **Pick up #2284 when a tag ships** — free 2× for any other deep ignored subtree; not worth a `replace` directive on unreleased `main` given #1 already solves this.
4. Prune `e2e/artifacts` in the canary task so 114 MB doesn't pile up regardless.

Hook wall time on your repo: **11.36s → 0.91s**

  5.257  ApplyTransition         0.123  ApplyTransition

## Fix 1 — `.gitignore` placement

Moved the rule to `e2e/.gitignore` as `artifacts/` so it's a direct child of its declaring `.gitignore`, which is the shape go-git can actually prune on. Left a comment in the root `.gitignore` explaining why it isn't there, since it looks like an accident otherwise. Git reports the directory as ignored either way (`e2e/.gitignore:10`).

New `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/status.go`. `gitrepo` was the right home — both `cli` and `strategy` already import it, it only depends on `paths`, and it's already the single source of truth for opening repos.

`gitrepo.Status(ctx, repo)` memoizes when the context carries a cache from `WithStatusCache`, keyed on worktree root (the two callers open the repo independently, so a pointer key wouldn't match). `handleLifecycleTurnStart` installs the cache.

scanned.

declare it in a `.gitignore` in its parent directory rather than as a nested
path from the root — reviewers should flag multi-component directory patterns
added to the root `.gitignore`.

# go-git: `gitignore.ReadPatterns` doesn't inherit ancestor patterns, so ignored subtrees aren't pruned

## The defect

`plumbing/format/gitignore/dir.go`, `ReadPatterns` (current `main`, `d6cbbfaa`):

```go
for _, fi := range fis {
    if fi.IsDir() && fi.Name() != gitDir {
        if NewMatcher(ps).Match(append(path, fi.Name()), true) {
            continue                                    // prune
        }
        subps, err = ReadPatterns(fs, append(path, fi.Name()))   // ← ps not passed
        ...
    }
}
```

The recursive call doesn't receive `ps`. Each level rebuilds its pattern set from only that directory's own ignore files, so the prune check can only ever match patterns declared by the directory currently being scanned.

**Consequence:** a rule prunes a subtree only when its target is a *direct child* of the `.gitignore` declaring it. Anything deeper never prunes.

- root `.gitignore` = `big/` → prunes at depth 0, because `big` is a direct child ✓
- root `.gitignore` = `outer/ignored/` → at root, `Match(["outer"])` fails (correctly); recursion into `outer/` starts with an empty `ps`; `Match(["outer","ignored"])` against nothing fails → **full descent** ✗

Reference git prunes both identically.

## Impact

`Worktree.Status()` → `collectIgnorePatterns()` → `ReadPatterns(w.filesystem, nil)` (`worktree_status.go:185`).

CPU profile of `Status()` on a synthetic repo (8,000 dirs under a root-declared `outer/ignored/`):

```
Duration: 606ms, samples 420ms
100%  Worktree.Status → collectIgnorePatterns → gitignore.ReadPatterns
 71%    └─ osfs.(*BoundOS).ReadDir
 29%    └─ osfs.openRootAt / validNoLeadingSymlink   (BoundOS traversal per call)
```

**`ReadPatterns` is the sole hot spot** — the diff walk contributes zero samples, because `diffStagingWithWorktree` hands the *full union* of patterns to `fsOpts.IgnoreMatcher` and the fs noder prunes correctly regardless of placement. So fixing `ReadPatterns` fixes `Status()` for this case; no second site to chase.

Real-world numbers from the Entire CLI repo (15,364 dirs in a root-ignored `e2e/artifacts/`), go-git `v6.0.0-alpha.5`:

| | time |
|---|---|
| `git status --porcelain` | 0.013s |
| `Worktree.Status()` | 5.25s |
| └─ `ReadPatterns` | 2.26s |
| `Status()` after moving the rule to `e2e/.gitignore` as `artifacts/` | **0.045s** |

That's ~116× from a one-line `.gitignore` move — which is the workaround I shipped in the CLI, and what your fix should make unnecessary.

## Relationship to #2284

#2284 (merged 2026-07-30, **unreleased** — `alpha.5` was tagged 2026-07-29 11:36, hours before the PR opened; still the newest tag) removed the blind `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` open attempts per directory. Measured A/B on the CLI repo:

| | ReadPatterns | Status |
|---|---|---|
| alpha.5 | 2.26s | 5.24s |
| main @ #2284 | 0.85s | 2.47s |

Real but partial — 2.1×. It makes each visited directory cheaper; it doesn't stop visiting 15k directories that should never be entered. The recursion is untouched.

Worth noting its benchmark can't catch this: `setupReadPatternsTree` puts ignore files at the root, which is exactly the placement that already prunes. A regression benchmark for this defect needs a *nested* pattern.

## The fix

Thread accumulated patterns into the recursion. Sketch:

```go
func ReadPatterns(fs billy.Filesystem, path []string) ([]Pattern, error) {
    return readPatterns(fs, path, nil)
}

func readPatterns(fs billy.Filesystem, path []string, inherited []Pattern) ([]Pattern, error) {
    // ... existing ReadDir + hasGitDir/hasGitignore logic ...
    // prune check matches against inherited + ps
}
```

Public API stays as-is. Two things worth getting right:

**Hoist the matcher.** `NewMatcher(ps)` is currently constructed *inside* the per-entry loop — a fresh matcher per subdirectory. Build it once per directory after patterns are collected.

**Negation is not a blocker.** I verified against reference git: with `outer/ignored/` plus `!outer/ignored/keep.txt`, git reports nothing and `check-ignore` attributes *both* files to the `outer/ignored/` rule. Per gitignore(5): *"It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded."* So pruning an excluded directory is precisely correct git semantics. Threading patterns down doesn't introduce a new risk class — it applies the *existing* prune logic to the cases it currently misses. Care is still needed for `foo/*` + `!foo/bar` (the directory itself isn't excluded, only its children), but that's already the current matcher's job.

**Behavioral note for the changelog:** this is observable beyond performance. Today, patterns from a nested `.gitignore` inside an ignored directory get collected into the returned set and can affect matching elsewhere; after pruning they won't be read at all. That matches git, but it is a semantic change, not purely an optimization.

## Suggested test/benchmark shape

- `BenchmarkReadPatterns/NestedIgnorePattern` — N dirs under a root-declared `outer/ignored/`; the gap vs `RootIgnoreFiles` is the whole bug.
- Deterministic regression test: count `ReadDir` calls through a counting `billy.Filesystem` and assert the ignored subtree is never entered. Better than wall-clock in CI.
- Equivalence test vs reference git across placements: `big/` at root, `outer/ignored/` at root, `ignored/` in `outer/.gitignore` — all three must produce the same ignore decisions.

## Upstream context

- #2284 — merged, the immediate predecessor; its description explicitly leaves *"the larger lazy/incremental pattern walk idea"* as future work. This is that work.
- #2282 and issue #181 — the profiling thread that surfaced `ReadPatterns` as ~28% of `Status()` CPU on a home-directory-style worktree.
